extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, registered patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners (Central Reexamination Unit)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for filing and processing requests for supplemental examination under 35 U.S.C. 257, and for any resulting ex parte reexamination. Covers who may file, required contents and format of requests, timing, determination criteria (substantial new question of patentability), effects, and related procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may request supplemental examination of a patent to consider, reconsider, or correct information believed to be relevant to the patent (35 U.S.C. 257).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination is a mechanism to have the Office consider any information (not limited to patents and printed publications) that the patent owner believes relevant to the patent, and may address any ground of patentability (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 101, anticipation, public use or sale, obviousness, written description, enablement, indefiniteness, double-patenting). The Office must conclude the supplemental examination within three months and issue a certificate indicating whether the information raises a substantial new question of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file (ownership requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for supplemental examination must be filed by the owner(s) of the entire right, title, and interest in the patent (37 CFR 1.601(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exclusive licensee or a person with proprietary interest under 35 U.S.C. 118 is not eligible. The request must identify the owner(s) and include a submission establishing entirety of ownership in compliance with 37 CFR 3.73(c) (see 37 CFR 1.610(b)(9)). All parties having an interest are deemed a composite patent owner and must act together unless a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is filed (e.g., deceased or incapacitated joint owner, or joint owner cannot be found after diligent effort). Court determination of ownership may be required for dissolved organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal representative filing and representation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal representative of the patent owner may file a request on behalf of the patent owner, but an attorney or agent representing the patent owner must be a registered patent practitioner and act under the appropriate authority (power of attorney under 37 CFR 1.32 or representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To act under 1.34 the practitioner must provide registration number, name, and signature. Power of attorney under 1.32 may name inventors or registered practitioners. A patent owner may not be represented by a non-registered person in supplemental examination or any resulting ex parte reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on third-party filing and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party other than the patent owner (i.e., any third party) is prohibited from filing papers or otherwise participating in any manner in a supplemental examination proceeding (37 CFR 1.601(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel should not discuss or answer inquiries from third parties about specific supplemental examination proceedings; third parties should be referred to the Central Reexamination Unit SPRS for strictly general procedural matters only. Ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 likewise excludes third-party participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to files and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not intend to provide public access to a request for supplemental examination or to papers submitted with the request until the request is granted a filing date; after filing date the supplemental examination file is open via Patent Center (non-patent literature cited will not be available via Patent Center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of the supplemental examination file or NPL must be ordered from the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch upon payment of applicable fees. Preferred ordering via Certified Copy Center storefront; email and fee payment options available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address and where Office directs communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence for supplemental examination is directed to the patent correspondence address of record in the patent file (37 CFR 1.33(c)); if the patent owner desires correspondence to be sent elsewhere, a change of correspondence address must be filed in the patent file and in the supplemental examination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the owner wants correspondence sent to a different registered attorney/agent than the one of record, a new power of attorney must be filed in both the patent file and the supplemental examination file (use of form PTO/AIA/81B encouraged). Papers must be signed by the patent owners or a registered attorney/agent of record or a representative under 1.34. The Office normally will not send duplicate correspondence to owner and attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney/agent: practitioner obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawing practitioner must take steps reasonably practicable to protect a client's interests (37 CFR 11.116(d)), such as giving reasonable notice, allowing time to employ other counsel, surrendering papers and property, and refunding unearned fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable notice should allow time for the client to seek other counsel prior to expiration of any applicable response period. Withdrawing practitioner(s) must request that correspondence be directed to the patent owner of record; they cannot change correspondence to another law firm's address or an address other than the patent owner of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file — separate submission and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for supplemental examination should be deposited as a new, separate, and independent submission and not be placed in the patent file or any other proceeding file; the request should be clearly identified (e.g., heading 'SUPPLEMENTAL EXAMINATION'). Use of form PTO/SB/59 'Request for Supplemental Examination Transmittal Form' is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination proceedings are distinct from any resulting ex parte reexamination; the supplemental proceeding is assigned a 'series 96' control number which is retained for any resulting reexamination. Any papers to be filed in a reexamination ordered as a result should be filed in the reexamination proceeding (follow-on papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners may submit requests and papers electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system; initial requests may be filed electronically by nonregistered users, but only registered users can file follow-on papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing is encouraged. For details see Patent Center User Guide; contact Patent Electronic Business Center for registration and filing assistance. Corrected requests responding to Notices of Noncompliant Requests should be filed as follow-on papers in existing proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper (hard copy) submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office accepts hard copy requests and other papers; paper submissions should be addressed to 'Mail Stop Supplemental Examination' and Mail Stop information should be prominent on first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All necessary address conventions for USPS vs hand-carried deliveries are specified and should include correct Mail Stop for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for supplemental examination and corrected requests may not be fax-transmitted; other papers (not requests or corrected requests) may be faxed in accordance with reexamination practice where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facsimile transmissions of papers to be filed in a resulting reexamination proceeding (except certain correspondence to Office of General Counsel) may be sent to the Central Reexamination Unit as permitted by reexamination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of papers (compliance with 37 CFR 1.52 and 1.615)
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers submitted in a supplemental examination proceeding must be formatted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.52; court documents and non-patent literature may be redacted but must be otherwise identical in content and format, and must not be reduced in size or modified (37 CFR 1.615).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents, patent application publications, and third-party-generated affidavits/declarations must not be reduced in size or otherwise modified. Noncompliance with 1.615 will render the request defective (see 37 CFR 1.610(d) and MPEP § 2812.01). Electronic filing is permitted per MPEP § 2806.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for requesting supplemental examination (period of enforceability)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent (37 CFR 1.601(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office set the enforceability period generally as expiration date plus six years, but it may be extended if litigation is pending within statutory limitations. The patent owner is responsible for determining patent expiration, considering maintenance fees, disclaimers, term adjustments/ extensions, and other relevant factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of items of information per request
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request may include no more than twelve items of information believed to be relevant to the patent (37 CFR 1.605(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than one request for the same patent may be filed at any time during enforceability. Items may be any evidence the owner believes relevant (not limited to patents/printed publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible scope of 'items of information'
rubrics_metrics.description: The information submitted may include any information the patent owner believes relevant to the patent; it is not limited to patents and printed publications (MPEP examples include sales invoices, transcripts of audio/video recordings, and any ground of patentability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items may involve patentable subject matter issues under 35 U.S.C. 101, anticipation, public use or sale, obviousness, written description, enablement, indefiniteness, and double-patenting. Ex parte reexamination ordered as a result is likewise not limited to patents and printed publications under 35 U.S.C. 257(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement — detailed explanation of relevance and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must include a detailed explanation of the relevance and the manner of applying each item of information to the patent (see MPEP heading 'Detailed Explanation of the Relevance and Manner of Applying Each Item of Information').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient detail should be provided so the examiner can determine whether each item raises a substantial new question of patentability. Optional additional content may be permitted but must comply with rules on unauthorized papers and limits on discussion of other proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information relating to correction of factual information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request includes information intended to correct factual information, the request should clearly identify and explain the correction and supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective factual submissions must still comply with formatting and content rules and count toward the item limit. Corrected requests responding to Notices of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request are filed as follow-on papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for supplemental examination and per-item fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall establish fees for submission of a request for supplemental examination and to consider each item of information submitted; if reexamination is ordered, ex parte reexamination fees are also payable (35 U.S.C. 257(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees and document-size fees are governed by regulations; reexamination fees applicable to ex parte reexamination under chapter 30 are required in addition to supplemental examination fees when reexamination is ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing, filing date, and noncompliant requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord a filing date to a compliant request; noncompliant (defective/improper) requests are handled per MPEP (e.g., Notice of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request) and a corrected request may be filed as follow-on paper(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request is defective and not corrected, it may be terminated due to defective/improper request. Certificate of mailing and Priority Mail Express procedures may be used for filing except for requests or corrected requests (see MPEP §§ 512, 513).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of papers other than a request (follow-on papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers other than the initial request should be rare in the supplemental examination proceeding; after reexamination is ordered, subsequent papers should be filed in the resulting reexamination proceeding as follow-on papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any correspondence relating to the proceeding should identify the patent number, control number, art unit, and examiner name. Follow-on papers require registered user access for electronic filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments restriction in resulting ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ex parte reexamination is ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257, the patent owner will not have the right to file a statement pursuant to 37 CFR 1.530 and may not file an amendment until after supplemental examination is concluded and after the issuance of an initial Office action on the merits (see 35 U.S.C. 257(b) and MPEP § 2818).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No patent owner statement under 1.530 will be solicited or accepted in reexaminations ordered under 257; amendments are restricted to preserve statutory procedures and timelines for ex parte reexamination ordered pursuant to supplemental examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews are prohibited in supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are prohibited in supplemental examination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination is a written submission/assessment process concluding with issuance of a certificate; any procedural contacts should be limited and follow CRU procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for deciding a supplemental examination request (three-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months after the date a request meeting requirements is received, the Director shall conduct the supplemental examination and shall conclude such examination by issuing a certificate indicating whether the information raises a substantial new question of patentability (35 U.S.C. 257(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-month statutory period governs supplemental examination conclusion and issuance of the supplemental examination certificate; this timing motivates the need for notices of other proceedings and limits on the scope of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination criterion — Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office must determine whether one or more items of information in the request raise a substantial new question of patentability; if so, reexamination shall be ordered (35 U.S.C. 257(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination addresses each item identified and the claims affected. The 'material to patentability' standard applicable is defined by 37 CFR 1.56(b) (read 'applicant' as 'patent owner' for supplemental examination). The reasons for determination must be provided in an accompanying reasons document and used to prepare an order for ex parte reexamination if SNQ is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered in making determination
rubrics_metrics.description: When making the determination whether a substantial new question of patentability exists, the examiner will consider which claims are affected and identify the claim(s) for which SNQ is found in the Statement of Reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resulting ex parte reexamination order will list the claims for which SNQ was found, per the Statement of Reasons, and the reexamination will address each SNQ identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the determination and issuance of supplemental examination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental examination certificate indicates whether the items presented raise a substantial new question of patentability and is accompanied by a reasons document explaining the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SNQ is found, the certificate will indicate reexamination will be ordered and the reasons document informs preparation of the ex parte reexamination order. If no SNQ is found, the certificate will be published as an attachment to the patent and reexamination fees (if paid) will be refunded as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on enforceability and statutory exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not be held unenforceable on the basis of conduct relating to information that had not been considered, was inadequately considered, or was incorrect in a prior examination if the information was considered, reconsidered, or corrected during supplemental examination (35 U.S.C. 257(c)(1)), subject to specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include prior allegations pled with particularity in civil actions or certain FDA notice conditions before the date of the supplemental examination request, and that in enforcement actions under section 337 or section 281 the defense based on information considered in supplemental examination will not apply unless the supplemental examination (and any reexamination ordered) are concluded before the action is brought (35 U.S.C. 257(c)(2)). Other statutory limitations on construction and sanctions remain in effect (35 U.S.C. 257(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and electronic issuance of the supplemental examination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental examination proceeding concludes with electronic issuance of a supplemental examination certificate (35 U.S.C. 257(a) and 37 CFR 1.625(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate will be published in due course as an attachment to the patent. If no SNQ is found, fees for reexamination (if paid) will be refunded per 37 CFR 1.20(k)(2) and 37 CFR 1.610(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure after conclusion — if SNQ found (order reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the determination finds a substantial new question of patentability, the Director shall order ex parte reexamination of the patent; the reexamination shall be conducted according to procedures established by chapter 30, with specific exceptions under 35 U.S.C. 257(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may use form PTO-2302 or include form paragraph 28.04 at the beginning of an initial Office action on the merits to order reexamination. The resulting reexamination will use the same control number as the supplemental examination for tracking, but is a distinct proceeding. The patent owner does not have the right to file a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 in such reexamination, and amendments are restricted until after the initial OA on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure after conclusion — if no SNQ found
rubrics_metrics.description: If the certificate indicates no substantial new question of patentability, the supplemental examination certificate will be published as an attachment to the patent and any reexamination fee paid will be refunded as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The issuance of a 'no SNQ' certificate has the statutory effect described in 35 U.S.C. 257(c) regarding considerations of previously unconsidered or incorrect information and enforceability, subject to exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of possible material fraud and referral
rubrics_metrics.description: If, during supplemental examination or any resulting reexamination, the Office becomes aware that a material fraud on the Office may have been committed in connection with the patent, the matter will continue to be processed and will be referred to the U.S. Attorney General in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 257(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such referrals are confidential, not included in the patent file, and not disclosed to the public unless the United States brings criminal charges. The Office anticipates such instances will be rare and does not intend to create a dedicated unit to investigate material fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of notification of other prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner must, as soon as possible upon discovery, file a paper limited to notifying the Office of any other prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceeding involving the patent (37 CFR 1.620(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be limited to identification of the proceeding (type, identifying number, filing date) and must not discuss issues or include copies of papers from the other proceeding; including discussion or papers will render it improper and it will be processed as an unauthorized paper under 37 CFR 1.620(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple post-patent Office proceedings and potential merging
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office generally will not merge supplemental examination proceedings but reserves the option to merge or consolidate proceedings as circumstances arise; any determination about which proceedings to initiate and order of initiation will be made case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination must conclude within three months of filing date. If reexamination is ordered, it must be conducted per chapter 30; the Office may provide for stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination under other statutory provisions when copending proceedings (e.g., IPR, PGR) exist. Petition to merge is generally unnecessary when the Office chooses to merge sua sponte.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of supplemental examination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination requests are assigned to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) based on the technology classification of the patent; CRU Supervisory Patent Examiner assigns the request to a primary examiner other than the original examiner who is most familiar with the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer procedures to another examiner will generally follow reexamination practice. The proceeding is assigned to the art unit corresponding to the patent's original classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 and under 35 U.S.C. 302
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 will be conducted under the regulations for ex parte reexamination except for enumerated differences: (1) patent owner will not have the right to file a statement under 37 CFR 1.530; (2) patent owner cannot file an amendment until supplemental examination is concluded and after issuance of an initial OA on the merits; (3) reexamination may be based on any item of information per 37 CFR 1.605 and is not limited to patents and printed publications; (4) issues beyond patents/printed publications may be considered; (5) material-to-patentability standard is defined by 37 CFR 1.56(b) for reexaminations resulting from supplemental examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These differences reflect statutory breadth of 35 U.S.C. 257(b) and the application of 1.56(b) (read 'applicant' as 'patent owner') rather than the narrower 1.555(b) standard used for reexaminations under 302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material-to-patentability standard applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Information material to patentability in a supplemental examination and any resulting ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 257 is defined by 37 CFR 1.56(b), which is the same standard applicable to patent applications (with 'applicant' read as 'patent owner').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because supplemental examination and resulting reexamination are not limited to patents and printed publications, the 1.56(b) standard (duty of disclosure/ materiality) governs. This differs from ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302, which uses 1.555(b) limited to patents and printed publications.
